newsitem.title: FRANCE: Syria, France discuss Middle East peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria, France discuss Middle East peace.

text.p: Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara discussed efforts to revive the Middle East peace process with President Jacques Chirac on Saturday and urged Israel to back up words about peace with actions.

"President Chirac confirmed that France would continue to cooperate with us to push forward the peace process, to relaunch it and put it on the right track," Shara said after meeting Chirac at the Elysee presidential palace.

"There are a lot of declarations by Israeli leaders...these declarations are mainly positive, but the important thing is to translate them into actions, stick to the principles of the peace process and start where we left off," he said.

Chirac received a hero's welcome in Syria when he toured the region last month but alienated the Israeli right by pleading for a Palestinian state, a bigger European role in peace talks and the return of occupied Arab land to Syria and Lebanon.

Shara said U.S. President Bill Clinton had sent an "encouraging message to Assad. It stressed his insistence to continue the peace process, push it forward and cooperate...to realise a just and lasting peace."
